Subject: SIG questionnaire: network & isolation clarifications

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for taking our SIG intake. We reviewed the network section and have two specific asks relating to Dedicated (Redwood Dedicated) vs Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments:

1) A single-page diagram that clearly marks the control plane, data plane, and any customer-managed network boundaries for both Dedicated and Private. We need to show where our traffic is in-scope vs Redwood-managed.
2) A short inventory of egress/ingress ports and protocols (L4) that are required for each deployment mode and how they are restricted (NSG/SG, proxy, egress ACL).

Could you provide these items and a short paragraph describing how isolation is achieved and audited (SOC 2 evidence points we can reference)?

We'd like the materials by EOD Monday (11/09) if possible. Attaching the SIG network template for reference.

Regards,
Alice Chen
Security Risk Manager
Veridian Health

Alice — thanks for the clear asks. Looping Ben and Karthik who own the Dedicated/Private designs and SOC 2 artifact mapping respectively.

High-level answer (short):
- Dedicated: customer sits behind their own tenant boundary in our GPU pools. Control plane (model routing, billing, API gateway) stays in Redwood-managed control plane; customer data for inference is isolated in tenant-specific namespaces and optional VNet peering. Egress is controlled via NAT/egress gateway and strict ACLs.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): control plane can be run in a customer-managed VPC (private control plane) or a fully air-gapped on-prem cluster. Data never traverses Redwood public endpoints in air-gapped mode; for VPC-hosted private deployments, we publish a minimal set of control-plane endpoints and rely on customer routing + mutual TLS.

I'll attach a first-pass one-page diagram and a CSV of port/ingress rules. Karthik, can you add the SOC 2 evidence pointers (which artifact IDs we should cite) and any audit frequency notes?

Deliverables attached: redwood-dedicated-private-isolation-diagram-v1.pdf; network-inventory-ports-20261107.csv

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Platform Security (acting)
Redwood Inference

Notes on ports/protocols (add to CSV):
- API/control plane (HTTPS 443) — inbound from customer to Redwood control-plane endpoints (for hosted control plane). For Private (VPC), control plane endpoints are optional and are whitelisted IP ranges or endpoint FQDNs communicated during onboarding.
- Model inference traffic (gRPC/HTTP) — for Dedicated, internal within Redwood GPU cluster (no public ingress). For Private VPC it traverses the customer-managed subnet; TLS enforced end-to-end.
- Egress to model updates / telemetry (443) — all telemetry is routed through an egress gateway with egress ACL. Customers can opt-out of telemetry in Private air-gapped installs.
- SSH management (TCP 22) — strictly restricted, jump hosts only; emergency access via ticket + recorded bastion session.

Security controls: subnet-level NSGs, host-based firewall rules, egress proxy with allowlist, and optional private peering for Dedicated. For Private we include a short checklist in the diagram showing which zones are customer-managed vs Redwood-managed.

Ben
Principal Product Engineer, Redwood Dedicated

Alice — adding the SOC 2 / SIG pointers requested. For the paragraph you asked for, you can cite the following artifacts during your SIG review: 

- SOC2-Audit-2026-Report (controls CC.DS and CC.APP; network segregation and change management sections).
- Config-Inventory-202611 (evidence of NSG/SG naming convention and applied rules).
- Network-Scan-202610 (quarterly vulnerability scans and egress rule verification results).

Suggested paragraph (feel free to paste into the SIG):
"Redwood Inference enforces network isolation for Dedicated and Private deployments through a combination of tenant-scoped namespaces, subnet-level access controls, and centrally managed egress gateways. Dedicated customers are placed into isolated compute pools with network policies that only permit necessary control plane communications; private deployments allow customers to operate a private control plane or an air-gapped on-prem cluster where Redwood does not receive inference payloads. Separation is validated via automated configuration scans (Config-Inventory-202611) and quarterly network scans (Network-Scan-202610), and is covered under our SOC 2 report (SOC2-Audit-2026-Report) for the applicable controls."

I also added the artifact IDs to the Drive link Lauren shared.

-Karthik
Head of Security Compliance

If you can add those two bullets to the Drive doc linked earlier we'll mark this item as resolved on our side. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Alice
